$comment: Structural spine. These are the grouping nodes that hold the per-subsystem fragments together, plus the three navigation entries that guarantee the deep trunks (metals, petrochemicals, industry) and the bundled/required-peripheral branches are reachable from the root even if no fragment references them by id. Three of the five are deliberately kind `note`: they are indexes, not things in the supply chain, and they keep their children because data/00-root.json references them by id and this pass does not own that file.

roots.name: Mainboard ASSY 250407
roots.description: A single two-layer FR-4 board carrying the whole computer: 1.6 mm of laminate with 35 um of copper on each face, about 1200 unplated component holes, and not one plated-through hole or via anywhere on it. Eight 4164 64 Kbit DRAMs give the 64 KB of main RAM and one 2114L static chip holds 1 KB of screen colour; a 6510 at about 1 MHz, the 6567 VIC-II, the 6581 SID, two 6526 CIAs, a mask-programmed 906114-01 PLA and three mask ROMs - 901226-01 BASIC, 901227-03 KERNAL and the 4 KB 901225-01 character generator - do the rest. Everything is through-hole DIP, so every connection between two parts is a copper trace: where a later revision has a via, this board carries a short single-core jumper wire soldered across the same pads. About 320 components in all: 18 memory, custom-logic and ROM devices, about a dozen 74-series glue parts, a few CMOS parts and a handful of small-signal transistors.

facts.label: Board
facts.value: ASSY 250407, PCB 326498-01, material no. 250406, artwork 251137, schematic 251138

facts.label: Jumper wires
facts.value: 2 (E1, E2) across pads where a later revision has a via

facts.label: Mask ROM
facts.value: 20 KB total: 8 KB BASIC + 8 KB KERNAL + 4 KB character generator

roots.note: The 250407 is the long 'breadbin' layout and the U-numbers quoted throughout this tree are its canonical set; they do not line up with the 250425, 250466 or short boards. The via count is the one a validated copy of the 250407 artwork settles: zero, which is why the zero-via claim is stated in the description rather than left as a footnote. This node no longer lists c64.connector-jacks or c64.mains among its children: the plugs belong to the panel they are soldered into, which c64.io-panel carries, and the line cord, plug, switch and fuse live in the external power supply, which is a separate assembly reached from the top of the tree.

roots.name: Connectors and operator controls
roots.description: Everything that plugs into the machine, and the one thing besides the keyboard a person touches to run it. The rear edge of the board carries the 44-pin cartridge expansion socket, the integral RF modulator with its channel adjust and RCA antenna socket, an 8-pin DIN for composite video plus separate luma and chroma and audio in and out, the 6-pin DIN serial bus, the 2 x 6 card-edge datasette port and the 24-pin card-edge user port, and the panel also takes a 7-pin DIN power input and two DE-9 control ports. Power arrives as 5 V DC and 9 V AC on that 7-pin socket rather than as mains, because the transformer, rectifier and regulators are in the external supply - which is why the machine's own earthing arrangement is an interwinding screen and a bond inside the brick. The operator control is a power rocker in the right-hand case panel. A breadbin C64 has no volume, tone or brightness controls: audio and video levels are fixed on the board.

facts.label: Video / audio
facts.value: 8-pin round DIN, 262-degree horseshoe: composite out, separate Y and C out, audio in and out

facts.label: Serial bus
facts.value: 6-pin round DIN, Commodore's serial variant of the IEEE-488 handshake, 300 baud

facts.label: Datasette
facts.value: 2 x 6 card edge: read, write, sense, motor, +5 V and ground

facts.label: User port
facts.value: 24-pin card edge: 17 TTL signals plus 7 ground and voltage pins, one of them 9 V AC

facts.label: Expansion
facts.value: 44-pin dual-row card edge carrying the CPU address and data buses

facts.label: Power input
facts.value: 7-pin round DIN: 5 V DC and 9 V AC from the external supply

facts.label: RF modulator
facts.value: integral on the breadbin; RCA antenna output, channel set on the board by a trimmer

roots.note: Checked against c64.connector-jacks, which carries one subtree per connector - user port, cassette port, expansion port, video/audio DIN, serial DIN, control ports and power inlet - plus the shared contact-stamping and housing-moulding sequences and one connector deliberately left off this list, the keyboard ribbon header, which is an internal board-to-board header rather than something a user plugs into. Two qualifications worth keeping: the earliest boards, PCB 326498, carry a 5-pin DIN video connector with composite and luminance but no chroma, the 8-pin part appearing part-way through production; and this subtree is listed once, here, rather than also hanging off the mainboard.
